```{r setup, include = FALSE}
source("01_preprocessing.R")   # same data prep as the scripts, so results match
library(flexdashboard)
library(shiny)

# fixed colours so an event looks the same on every page
palette_main  <- c("#2A9D8F", "#E76F51", "#1F3A5F", "#E9C46A")
event_colours <- c("Censored" = "#B8C4CE", "Relapse" = "#E76F51",
                   "Death before relapse" = "#1F3A5F")
method_colours <- c("Aalen-Johansen" = "#2A9D8F", "1 - Kaplan-Meier" = "#E76F51")

theme_dashboard <- theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
        panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#E5E9F0"),
        legend.position  = "bottom",
        legend.title     = element_blank(),
        axis.title       = element_text(colour = "#4A5568"),
        axis.text        = element_text(colour = "#4A5568"),
        strip.text       = element_text(face = "bold", colour = "#1F3A5F", size = 13))

# menu label = column name in the data
explore_choices <- c(
  "Patient age (years)" = "patient_age",
  "Donor age (years)"   = "donor_age",
  "Waiting time (days)" = "waiting_days",
  "Patient sex"         = "patient_sex",
  "Patient CMV"         = "patient_cmv",
  "Donor CMV"           = "donor_cmv",
  "MTX given"           = "mtx",
  "First event"         = "event_label"
)

group_choices <- c(
  "Disease group" = "disease_group",
  "Patient sex"   = "patient_sex",
  "Patient CMV"   = "patient_cmv",
  "Donor CMV"     = "donor_cmv",
  "MTX given"     = "mtx"
)

# models don't depend on inputs, so fit them once at start-up
cox_relapse <- coxph(Surv(time, relapse_event) ~ disease_group + age10 + patient_sex,data = analysis_data)
cox_summary <- summary(cox_relapse)

# crr() only takes a numeric matrix, so factors become 0/1 columns
fg_covariates <- model.matrix(~ disease_group + age10 + patient_sex,
                              data = analysis_data)[, -1]
fg_relapse <- crr(ftime = analysis_data$time, fstatus = analysis_data$event_status,
                  cov1 = fg_covariates, failcode = 1, cencode = 0)
fg_summary <- summary(fg_relapse)

model_results <- data.frame(
  Variable  = term_labels[colnames(fg_covariates)],
  HR        = cox_summary$conf.int[, "exp(coef)"],
  HR_lower  = cox_summary$conf.int[, "lower .95"],
  HR_upper  = cox_summary$conf.int[, "upper .95"],
  HR_p      = cox_summary$coefficients[, "Pr(>|z|)"],
  SHR       = fg_summary$conf.int[, 1],
  SHR_lower = fg_summary$conf.int[, 3],
  SHR_upper = fg_summary$conf.int[, 4],
  SHR_p     = fg_summary$coef[, 5],
  row.names = NULL
)

ph_test <- cox.zph(cox_relapse)$table

cif_all  <- cuminc(analysis_data$time, analysis_data$event_status, cencode = 0)
naive_km <- survfit(Surv(time, relapse_event) ~ 1, data = analysis_data)   # kept only to show the bias
```

  geom_bar(position = "fill", width = 0.6) +

### About this dashboard

**Question.** After a bone marrow transplant, which patients are more likely to relapse, and how should relapse risk be measured when some patients die first?

**Data.** 137 patients with acute leukaemia (dataset `bmt`, R package KMsurv). For each patient the first of three outcomes is recorded: relapse, death before relapse (a competing event), or censoring.

**Pages.**

- **Data** - explore any variable by group
- **Survival** - Kaplan-Meier curves and the log-rank test
- **Competing risks** - cumulative incidence (Aalen-Johansen), Gray's test, and why 1 - Kaplan-Meier overestimates relapse
- **Models** - cause-specific Cox and Fine-Gray regression
- **Simulation** - test both estimators against a known true value

Survival {data-orientation=columns}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=280}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Overall survival**

```{r}
selectInput("km_group", "Compare by", choices = group_choices)
checkboxInput("km_ci", "Show 95% confidence intervals", value = FALSE)
```

Kaplan-Meier estimate of the probability of being alive. The log-rank test checks whether the curves differ between groups.

```{r}
# shared by the plot and the one-year table, so it is fitted once
km_fit <- reactive({
  survfit(as.formula(paste("Surv(os_days, died) ~", input$km_group)),
          data = analysis_data)
})

logrank <- reactive({
  survdiff(as.formula(paste("Surv(os_days, died) ~", input$km_group)),
           data = analysis_data)
})
```

Column {data-width=650}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Kaplan-Meier curves

```{r}
renderPlot({
  fit <- km_fit()

  # ggplot needs a data frame, not a survfit object
  curves <- data.frame(
    time     = fit$time,
    survival = fit$surv,
    lower    = fit$lower,
    upper    = fit$upper,
    censored = fit$n.censor > 0,
    group    = sub(".*=", "", rep(names(fit$strata), fit$strata))
  )
  # every curve starts at 100% on day 0
  start  <- data.frame(time = 0, survival = 1, lower = 1, upper = 1,
                       censored = FALSE, group = unique(curves$group))
  curves <- rbind(start, curves)
  curves$group <- factor(curves$group, levels = levels(analysis_data[[input$km_group]]))   # keep legend order

  plot <- ggplot(curves, aes(x = time, y = survival, colour = group)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_point(data = subset(curves, censored), shape = 3, size = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = palette_main) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = function(x) paste0(x * 100, "%")) +
    labs(x = "Days since transplant", y = "Survival probability") +
    theme_dashboard

  if (input$km_ci) {
    plot <- plot +
      geom_step(aes(y = lower), linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
      geom_step(aes(y = upper), linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  plot
})
```

### Log-rank test

```{r}
renderUI({
  test    <- logrank()
  df      <- length(test$n) - 1
  p_value <- pchisq(test$chisq, df = df, lower.tail = FALSE)
  verdict <- if (p_value < 0.05) "Survival differs between groups." else
    "No clear evidence that survival differs between groups."
  HTML(sprintf("<p style='font-size:16px'>Chi-square = <b>%.2f</b> on %d df<br>
                p-value = <b>%.4f</b></p><p>%s</p>",
               test$chisq, df, p_value, verdict))
})
```

Competing risks {data-orientation=columns}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=280}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Relapse vs death**

```{r}
selectInput("cif_group", "Compare by", choices = group_choices)
sliderInput("cif_day", "Estimate at day", min = 0, max = 2000, value = 365, step = 50)
```

Death before relapse is a competing event: after death, relapse cannot occur. The cumulative incidence (Aalen-Johansen) accounts for this; 1 - Kaplan-Meier treats deaths as censored and overestimates relapse.

```{r}
cif_fit <- reactive({
  cuminc(ftime   = analysis_data$time,
         fstatus = analysis_data$event_status,
         group   = analysis_data[[input$cif_group]],
         cencode = 0)
})
```

Column {data-width=600}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Cumulative incidence by group

```{r}
renderPlot({
  fit <- cif_fit()

  # curve names look like "ALL 1": group, then cause (1 relapse, 2 death)
  cif_curves <- data.frame()
  for (curve_name in names(fit)) {
    if (curve_name == "Tests") next
    cif_curves <- rbind(cif_curves, data.frame(
      group    = sub(" [12]$", "", curve_name),
      cause    = ifelse(grepl("1$", curve_name), "Relapse", "Death before relapse"),
      time     = fit[[curve_name]]$time,
      estimate = fit[[curve_name]]$est
    ))
  }
  cif_curves$group <- factor(cif_curves$group, levels = levels(analysis_data[[input$cif_group]]))
  cif_curves$cause <- factor(cif_curves$cause, levels = c("Relapse", "Death before relapse"))

  ggplot(cif_curves, aes(x = time, y = estimate, colour = group)) +
    geom_step(linewidth = 1.1) +
    geom_vline(xintercept = input$cif_day, linetype = "dotted", colour = "#6C7A89") +
    facet_wrap(~ cause) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = palette_main) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = function(x) paste0(x * 100, "%")) +
    labs(x = "Days since transplant", y = "Cumulative incidence") +
    theme_dashboard
})
```

Models
=====================================

Row {data-height=550}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Effect of patient characteristics on relapse

```{r}
forest <- rbind(
  data.frame(model = "Cause-specific Cox (HR)", variable = model_results$Variable,
             ratio = model_results$HR, lower = model_results$HR_lower,
             upper = model_results$HR_upper),
  data.frame(model = "Fine-Gray (SHR)", variable = model_results$Variable,
             ratio = model_results$SHR, lower = model_results$SHR_lower,
             upper = model_results$SHR_upper)
)

ggplot(forest, aes(x = variable, y = ratio, colour = model)) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 1, linetype = "dashed", colour = "#6C7A89") +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper),
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5), size = 0.6) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("#1F3A5F", "#E76F51")) +
  scale_y_log10() +
  coord_flip() +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "Ratio with 95% confidence interval (log scale)") +
  theme_dashboard
```

### How to read the models

**Cause-specific Cox (HR):** effect on the relapse *rate* among patients still alive and relapse-free. Deaths are treated as censored.

**Fine-Gray (SHR):** effect on the overall *probability* of relapse. Patients who died stay in the risk set as never relapsed.

A value above 1 means higher risk, below 1 lower risk. If the confidence interval crosses the dashed line at 1, the effect is not statistically significant.

Reference groups: ALL (disease group) and female (sex). Age is per 10 years.

Simulation {data-orientation=columns}
=====================================

Column {.sidebar data-width=280}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

**Simulation settings**

```{r}
sliderInput("sim_death", "Death rate (competing event)", min = 0, max = 0.30,
            value = 0.08, step = 0.02)
sliderInput("sim_censor", "Censoring rate", min = 0.02, max = 0.30,
            value = 0.05, step = 0.02)
sliderInput("sim_reps", "Number of simulated datasets", min = 50, max = 300,
            value = 100, step = 50)
actionButton("sim_run", "Run simulation", class = "btn-primary")
```

Each dataset has 137 patients and a relapse rate of 0.08. Both methods estimate the probability of relapse by time 5 and are compared with the true value. Try a death rate of 0, then 0.30.

```{r}
# runs on button click only, because the loop is slow
sim_results <- eventReactive(input$sim_run, {
  n_patients   <- 137
  relapse_rate <- 0.08
  tau          <- 5
  true_cif <- relapse_rate / (relapse_rate + input$sim_death) *
    (1 - exp(-(relapse_rate + input$sim_death) * tau))

  aj_estimates    <- numeric(input$sim_reps)
  naive_estimates <- numeric(input$sim_reps)

  withProgress(message = "Simulating", value = 0, {
    for (r in seq_len(input$sim_reps)) {
      time_relapse  <- rexp(n_patients, relapse_rate)
      time_death    <- rexp(n_patients, input$sim_death)
      time_censor   <- rexp(n_patients, input$sim_censor)
      observed_time <- pmin(time_relapse, time_death, time_censor)   # first event wins
      status <- ifelse(observed_time == time_relapse, 1,
                       ifelse(observed_time == time_death, 2, 0))

      aj_estimates[r] <- timepoints(cuminc(observed_time, status, cencode = 0), tau)$est[1, 1]
      km <- survfit(Surv(observed_time, status == 1) ~ 1)   # deaths treated as censored
      naive_estimates[r] <- 1 - summary(km, times = tau, extend = TRUE)$surv

      incProgress(1 / input$sim_reps)
    }
  })

  data.frame(method   = rep(c("Aalen-Johansen", "1 - Kaplan-Meier"), each = input$sim_reps),
             estimate = c(aj_estimates, naive_estimates),
             true_cif = true_cif)
}, ignoreNULL = FALSE)   # also run once at start so the page isn't empty
```

Column {data-width=650}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Estimated probability of relapse at time 5

```{r}
renderPlot({
  sims <- sim_results()
  ggplot(sims, aes(x = method, y = estimate, fill = method)) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.5, alpha = 0.85, outlier.size = 0.8) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = sims$true_cif[1], colour = "#1F3A5F", linewidth = 1) +
    annotate("text", x = 0.6, y = sims$true_cif[1], label = "true value",
             vjust = -0.6, hjust = 0, colour = "#1F3A5F") +
    scale_fill_manual(values = method_colours) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Estimate") +
    theme_dashboard +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
})
```

Column {data-width=350}
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

### Performance

```{r}
renderTable({
  sim_results() %>%
    group_by(Method = method) %>%
    summarise(`True value`    = mean(true_cif),
              `Mean estimate` = mean(estimate, na.rm = TRUE),
              Bias            = mean(estimate - true_cif, na.rm = TRUE),
              RMSE            = sqrt(mean((estimate - true_cif)^2, na.rm = TRUE)))
}, striped = TRUE, hover = TRUE, width = "100%", digits = 4)
```

### Reading the result

**Bias** is the average error (0 is ideal). **RMSE** is the typical size of the error.

The Aalen-Johansen estimate should sit on the true value. The 1 - Kaplan-Meier estimate is too high, and the gap grows as the death rate increases.
